Safemarch DNS & Identity Provider Lab

Build a reusable two-VM BIND9 + Keycloak OIDC identity foundation for Zscaler Authentication Service.

2 virtual machinesBIND9 + split DNSKeycloak + PostgreSQLnginx + trusted HTTPSOIDC + JIT + groups
DNS → HTTPS → OIDC → Zscaler
Orientation

Lab Structure

The final design needs only two virtual machines. The Ubuntu VM is both the Office DNS resolver and the identity platform; the Windows VM is the client used to validate DNS, HTTPS, OIDC and Zscaler Client Connector authentication.

Two-VM lab layout
1 — Ubuntu & NetworkStatic IP, hostname, packages and firewall. 2 — BIND9 DNSInternal Safemarch zone and recursive Office DNS. 3 — Docker & KeycloakPersistent PostgreSQL-backed Keycloak stack. 4 — Identity ModelRealm, users, groups and reusable Zscaler login attribute. 5 — HTTPS & Split DNSOwned public FQDN, nginx, Let's Encrypt and internal override. 6 — Zscaler OIDCPrimary IdP, confidential client and JIT provisioning. 7 — GroupsFinance/Marketing membership carried through OIDC. 8 — Session AttributesOptional department and employeeType session claims. TroubleshootingSymptoms and fixes learned during the build.
Before You Begin

Prerequisites, Variables and Design Rules

VM 1 — WindowsWindows 10/11 client on the Office network. Validated address: 192.168.1.1. Install Zscaler Client Connector when you reach federation testing.
VM 2 — UbuntuUbuntu 22.04 with console access and Internet egress. Final address: 192.168.1.252/24.
Public DNS ownershipControl of rupakdey.in (validated through GoDaddy) so idp.rupakdey.in can be published.
Zscaler tenantAuthentication Service access, a user domain, an available hosted *.zslogin.net admin namespace, and ZCC/ZPA entitlements when those services are tested.
Screenshot rule: Zscaler tenant names, user domains, vanity domains, IDs and redirect URIs visible in screenshots are reference values from the environment used during validation. Always use the values generated by the tenant you are configuring. The written variables and checkpoints in this guide take precedence over screenshot-specific tenant data.
VariableValidated / Example ValuePurpose
IDP_IP192.168.1.252Ubuntu DNS/IdP address.
OFFICE_NET192.168.1.0/24BIND query/recursion ACL and trusted lab subnet.
MGMT_PC192.168.1.1Windows client; only host allowed to SSH and temporarily reach 8080.
OFFICE_IFACEDiscover with ip -br addrUbuntu NIC used in Netplan.
OFFICE_GWDiscover with ip routePreserve the working DHCP gateway; do not guess it.
INTERNAL_DOMAINsafemarch.comInternal lab namespace.
INTERNAL_IDPidp.safemarch.comEarly internal smoke-test name.
PUBLIC_IDP_FQDNidp.rupakdey.inCanonical HTTPS/OIDC issuer used everywhere after Module 5.
SKYTAP_PUBLIC_FQDNidp.zscaler.skytapdns.comSkytap dynamic public service targeted by the public CNAME.
ZSCALER_DOMAINrdey.zscaler.netValidated Zscaler end-user/login domain. Replace for another tenant.
ZSCALER_VANITYrdey.zslogin.netValidated Authentication Service vanity/redirect host. Tenant-specific.
REALMSafemarchKeycloak realm.
OIDC_CLIENTzscaler-authentication-service-rdeyConfidential Keycloak client for the current tenant. Create a separate client per Zscaler tenant.
Keep the identity namespaces separatesafemarch.com is the internal/user identity namespace, idp.rupakdey.in is the public Keycloak issuer, and rdey.zscaler.net is the example Zscaler login domain. Do not try to make one name serve all three purposes.
Target name resolution and OIDC path
Windows / ZCCidp.rupakdey.in resolves internally to 192.168.1.252.
→
UbuntuBIND9 :53 · nginx :443 · Keycloak :8080 loopback · PostgreSQL
←

Module 1

Prepare Ubuntu and Configure the Static Office IP

InfrastructureFoundational45–60 min
GoalStart with a generic Ubuntu 22.04 VM using DHCP and finish with hostname idp, static address 192.168.1.252/24, preserved gateway, Internet access and a restrictive host firewall.

1. Record the working DHCP configuration

Use the Skytap console if possible. Changing a remote host address can interrupt SSH, so capture the current interface and route first.

hostname
hostname -I
ip -br addr
ip route
resolvectl status
ls -l /etc/netplan/

Write down the active interface and default gateway. Use the values from your VM, not a copied example.

2. Set the hostname

sudo hostnamectl set-hostname idp
hostname

3. Convert the NIC from DHCP to a static address

Back up the active Netplan file:

ls -l /etc/netplan/
sudo cat /etc/netplan/*.yaml
sudo cp /etc/netplan/<current-file>.yaml /etc/netplan/<current-file>.yaml.bak
sudo nano /etc/netplan/<current-file>.yaml

Use the interface and gateway recorded above. Preserve an existing renderer: line if the file has one.

network:
  version: 2
  ethernets:
    <OFFICE_IFACE>:
      dhcp4: false
      addresses:
        - 192.168.1.252/24
      routes:
        - to: default
          via: <OFFICE_GW>
      nameservers:
        addresses:
          - 1.1.1.1
          - 8.8.8.8
YAML mattersNetplan is indentation-sensitive. Use spaces, not tabs. Copy the working DHCP gateway exactly.
sudo netplan generate
sudo netplan try
# Confirm only after console connectivity is proven.
sudo netplan apply
ip -br addr
ip route
ping -c 3 1.1.1.1
getent hosts google.com

4. Install the base utilities

sudo apt update
sudo apt full-upgrade -y
sudo apt install -y curl wget vim jq dnsutils bind9 bind9-utils ufw nginx certbot python3-certbot-nginx ca-certificates openssl

5. Apply the host firewall

sudo ufw default deny incoming
sudo ufw default allow outgoing
sudo ufw allow from 192.168.1.1 to any port 22 proto tcp
sudo ufw allow from 192.168.1.0/24 to any port 53 proto udp
sudo ufw allow from 192.168.1.0/24 to any port 53 proto tcp
sudo ufw allow 80/tcp
sudo ufw allow 443/tcp
sudo ufw enable
sudo ufw status numbered
Do not expose Keycloak :8080 publiclyThe early smoke test temporarily publishes TCP/8080. Keep the VM private until Keycloak is moved to loopback and nginx is the only public front end.
Checkpointhostname returns idp; the Office NIC is 192.168.1.252/24; the original default gateway remains; Internet IP and DNS tests succeed.
Module 2

Configure BIND9 as the Office DNS Resolver

DNSModerate35–50 min
GoalMake 192.168.1.252 the Office DNS resolver, authoritative for the internal safemarch.com zone while forwarding unrelated names to public resolvers.

1. Configure BIND options

sudo cp /etc/bind/named.conf.options /etc/bind/named.conf.options.bak
sudo nano /etc/bind/named.conf.options
acl "office_clients" {
    127.0.0.1;
    192.168.1.0/24;
};

options {
    directory "/var/cache/bind";
    listen-on { 127.0.0.1; 192.168.1.252; };
    listen-on-v6 { none; };
    recursion yes;
    allow-query { office_clients; };
    allow-recursion { office_clients; };
    forwarders { 1.1.1.1; 8.8.8.8; };
    dnssec-validation auto;
};

2. Add the internal Safemarch zone

sudo nano /etc/bind/named.conf.local
zone "safemarch.com" {
    type primary;
    file "/etc/bind/db.safemarch.com";
};
sudo nano /etc/bind/db.safemarch.com
$TTL 300
@   IN  SOA idp.safemarch.com. admin.safemarch.com. (
        2026092701 ; increment whenever the zone changes
        3600
        900
        604800
        300
)
    IN  NS  idp.safemarch.com.
idp IN  A   192.168.1.252
Authoritative parent-zone cautionIf another DNS service already owns child names such as *.training.safemarch.com, do not assume BIND will recurse for them after becoming authoritative for safemarch.com. Add the required records or use a deliberate delegation/forwarding design.

3. Validate and start BIND

sudo named-checkconf
sudo named-checkzone safemarch.com /etc/bind/db.safemarch.com
sudo systemctl restart bind9
sudo systemctl enable bind9
sudo systemctl status bind9 --no-pager

4. Test authoritative and recursive resolution

dig @127.0.0.1 idp.safemarch.com +short
dig @192.168.1.252 idp.safemarch.com +short
dig @192.168.1.252 google.com +short
sudo ss -lunpt | grep ':53' || true

5. Point Windows to the new DNS server

Set the Windows adapter's DNS server to 192.168.1.252. Then:

nslookup idp.safemarch.com 192.168.1.252
nslookup www.google.com 192.168.1.252
CheckpointThe Windows endpoint resolves both idp.safemarch.com and public Internet names through 192.168.1.252.
Module 3

Install Docker and Build Persistent Keycloak

KeycloakModerate45–60 min
GoalProve Keycloak on the internal network, then replace the disposable test with a persistent PostgreSQL-backed deployment.

1. Install Docker and Compose

sudo apt update
sudo apt install -y docker.io
sudo systemctl enable --now docker
sudo systemctl status docker --no-pager
docker --version
docker compose version

If Compose v2 is missing:

sudo apt install -y docker-compose-v2

2. Allow the lab administrator to use Docker

sudo docker ps
sudo usermod -aG docker "$USER"
newgrp docker
docker ps
groups
Privilege noteMembership in the docker group is effectively root-equivalent on this lab host.

3. Run a disposable Keycloak smoke test

sudo ufw allow from 192.168.1.1 to any port 8080 proto tcp

docker run --rm   --name keycloak-test   -p 192.168.1.252:8080:8080   -e KC_BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_USERNAME=admin   -e KC_BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD='Replace-With-Strong-Password'   quay.io/keycloak/keycloak:26.7.4   start-dev

From Windows browse to http://idp.safemarch.com:8080. Sign in with the bootstrap admin, then stop the container with Ctrl+C. Do not build the realm in this disposable container.

4. Create the persistent Keycloak + PostgreSQL stack

sudo mkdir -p /opt/keycloak
sudo chown "$USER":"$USER" /opt/keycloak
cd /opt/keycloak
nano .env
POSTGRES_DB=keycloak
POSTGRES_USER=keycloak
POSTGRES_PASSWORD=<STRONG_DATABASE_PASSWORD>
KEYCLOAK_ADMIN=admin
KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_PASSWORD=<STRONG_KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_PASSWORD>
chmod 600 /opt/keycloak/.env
nano /opt/keycloak/compose.yaml
services:
  postgres:
    image: postgres:16-alpine
    container_name: keycloak-postgres
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      POSTGRES_DB: ${POSTGRES_DB}
      POSTGRES_USER: ${POSTGRES_USER}
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${POSTGRES_PASSWORD}
    volumes:
      - postgres_data:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U ${POSTGRES_USER} -d ${POSTGRES_DB}"]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 5

  keycloak:
    image: quay.io/keycloak/keycloak:26.7.4
    container_name: keycloak
    restart: unless-stopped
    depends_on:
      postgres:
        condition: service_healthy
    environment:
      KC_DB: postgres
      KC_DB_URL: jdbc:postgresql://postgres:5432/${POSTGRES_DB}
      KC_DB_USERNAME: ${POSTGRES_USER}
      KC_DB_PASSWORD: ${POSTGRES_PASSWORD}
      KC_BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_USERNAME: ${KEYCLOAK_ADMIN}
      KC_BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD: ${KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_PASSWORD}
    command: ["start-dev"]
    ports:
      - "192.168.1.252:8080:8080"

volumes:
  postgres_data:
cd /opt/keycloak
docker compose up -d
docker compose ps
docker compose logs --tail=80 keycloak

Reopen http://idp.safemarch.com:8080, then restart the stack and reboot once to prove persistence.

docker compose restart
sudo reboot
# After reboot:
cd /opt/keycloak && docker compose ps
CheckpointPostgreSQL is healthy and Keycloak is running after reboot. The realm can now be built without losing state.
Module 4

Create the Safemarch Realm, Users, Groups and Attributes

Identity ModelModerate45–60 min
GoalBuild a small identity source that is reusable across Zscaler tenants. Keep the built-in master realm for administration and create all lab end users in the Safemarch realm.

1. Create the realm

Open http://idp.safemarch.com:8080/admin/. Use the realm selector → Create realm and create Safemarch. Under Realm settings → Login, keep self-registration and email verification disabled unless mail infrastructure is available.

2. Create groups and users

UserKeycloak username / emailGroup
Maya Shahmaya.shah@safemarch.comFinance
Daniel Leedaniel.lee@safemarch.comMarketing

Give each user a non-temporary lab password.

3. Define managed user-profile attributes

Go to Realm settings → User profile → Attributes and create:

AttributeDisplay nameExample
departmentDepartmentMaya = Finance; Daniel = Marketing
employeeTypeEmployee TypeEmployee
zscaler_loginZscaler Loginmaya.shah@rdey.zscaler.net

4. Make zscaler_login controlled but tenant-flexible

MultivaluedOff
Enabled whenAlways
Required fieldOn
Required forUsers and admins
Who can editAdmin only
Who can viewUser + Admin

Use the built-in email validator. Do not add a tenant-specific regular expression. The master IdP is intentionally reusable across tenant domains, so a hard-coded @rdey.zscaler.net or older training-tenant pattern would make future migrations harder.

5. Populate the current sample users

UserNormal identityGroupdepartmentemployeeTypezscaler_login
Mayamaya.shah@safemarch.comFinanceFinanceEmployeemaya.shah@rdey.zscaler.net
Danieldaniel.lee@safemarch.comMarketingMarketingEmployeedaniel.lee@rdey.zscaler.net

6. Enable user-event logging

Go to Realm settings → Events → User events settings and enable event storage. Login, login-error, logout and code-to-token events are especially useful during OIDC troubleshooting.

7. Validate local authentication

Use the Account Console:

http://idp.safemarch.com:8080/realms/Safemarch/account/

Log in as Maya, log out, then repeat as Daniel. Confirm successful LOGIN events.

CheckpointBoth users authenticate locally; Finance/Marketing membership and the managed attributes are populated before federation is introduced.
Module 5

Publish Keycloak Through nginx and Build Split DNS

HTTPSDNSImportant60–75 min
GoalMake https://idp.rupakdey.in the single canonical Keycloak identity. Internet clients reach the Skytap public service; Office clients use split DNS to reach 192.168.1.252 directly while preserving the same hostname and certificate.

1. Bind Keycloak to loopback

Edit /opt/keycloak/compose.yaml:

ports:
  - "127.0.0.1:8080:8080"
cd /opt/keycloak
docker compose down
docker compose up -d
curl -I http://127.0.0.1:8080
sudo ufw delete allow from 192.168.1.1 to any port 8080 proto tcp

From Windows, Test-NetConnection 192.168.1.252 -Port 8080 should now fail.

2. Configure the initial nginx reverse proxy

sudo nano /etc/nginx/sites-available/keycloak
server {
    listen 80;
    server_name idp.safemarch.com;

    location / {
        proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:8080;
        proxy_http_version 1.1;
        proxy_set_header Host $host;
        proxy_set_header X-Real-IP $remote_addr;
        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;
        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;
        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Host $host;
        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Port $server_port;
    }
}
sudo ln -s /etc/nginx/sites-available/keycloak /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/keycloak
sudo rm -f /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/default
sudo nginx -t
sudo systemctl enable --now nginx
sudo systemctl reload nginx

3. Attach the Skytap dynamic public service

In Skytap open the Ubuntu VM → Network Adapters → Add service → Public IP (dynamic). The validated dynamic hostname is idp.zscaler.skytapdns.com. Keep TCP/80 and TCP/443 reachable for the public service.

4. Publish the owned canonical hostname

In the public DNS provider for rupakdey.in (validated with GoDaddy), create:

TypeNameTarget
CNAMEidpidp.zscaler.skytapdns.com

Verify with an external resolver:

dig @1.1.1.1 idp.rupakdey.in
# Expected chain: idp.rupakdey.in CNAME idp.zscaler.skytapdns.com → Skytap public IPv4

5. Issue the trusted certificate for idp.rupakdey.in

Change the nginx port-80 server_name to the canonical host, validate and reload:

server_name idp.rupakdey.in;

sudo nginx -t
sudo systemctl reload nginx
sudo certbot --nginx -d idp.rupakdey.in

If certificate issuance succeeds but installation fails because Certbot cannot find the server block, correct server_name, reload nginx and run:

sudo certbot install --cert-name idp.rupakdey.in

6. Switch Keycloak to production mode with the canonical hostname

Keep the PostgreSQL settings and update the Keycloak service:

environment:
  KC_DB: postgres
  KC_DB_URL: jdbc:postgresql://postgres:5432/${POSTGRES_DB}
  KC_DB_USERNAME: ${POSTGRES_USER}
  KC_DB_PASSWORD: ${POSTGRES_PASSWORD}
  KC_BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_USERNAME: ${KEYCLOAK_ADMIN}
  KC_BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD: ${KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_PASSWORD}
  KC_HOSTNAME: https://idp.rupakdey.in
  KC_HTTP_ENABLED: "true"
  KC_PROXY_HEADERS: xforwarded

command: ["start"]
ports:
  - "127.0.0.1:8080:8080"

In the nginx HTTPS server, make the original HTTPS scheme explicit:

location / {
    proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:8080;
    proxy_http_version 1.1;
    proxy_set_header Host $host;
    proxy_set_header X-Real-IP $remote_addr;
    proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;
    proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto https;
    proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Host $host;
    proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Port 443;
}
cd /opt/keycloak
docker compose down
docker compose up -d
sudo nginx -t
sudo systemctl reload nginx

7. Validate canonical OIDC metadata externally

curl -I https://idp.rupakdey.in
curl -s https://idp.rupakdey.in/realms/Safemarch/.well-known/openid-configuration   | jq '{issuer,authorization_endpoint,token_endpoint,userinfo_endpoint,jwks_uri}'

Every endpoint must begin with https://idp.rupakdey.in/. There should be no 127.0.0.1, 192.168.1.252, :8080, idp.safemarch.com or http:// in the discovery document.

8. Add a narrow split-DNS zone for the exact public IdP FQDN

The Skytap Office network did not provide a usable hairpin path to its own public service. Keep the public CNAME externally, but make BIND authoritative only for the exact hostname idp.rupakdey.in internally.

sudo nano /etc/bind/named.conf.local
zone "idp.rupakdey.in" {
    type primary;
    file "/etc/bind/db.idp.rupakdey.in";
};
sudo nano /etc/bind/db.idp.rupakdey.in
$TTL 300
@   IN  SOA idp.rupakdey.in. admin.rupakdey.in. (
        2026092701
        3600
        900
        604800
        300
)
    IN  NS  idp.rupakdey.in.
    IN  A   192.168.1.252
sudo named-checkconf
sudo named-checkzone idp.rupakdey.in /etc/bind/db.idp.rupakdey.in
sudo rndc reconfig
sudo rndc zonestatus idp.rupakdey.in
dig @192.168.1.252 idp.rupakdey.in

The answer should be 192.168.1.252 and include the aa flag.

9. Validate Windows and browser DNS behavior

ipconfig /flushdns
Resolve-DnsName idp.rupakdey.in
Test-NetConnection idp.rupakdey.in -Port 443

Then open https://idp.rupakdey.in/realms/Safemarch/account/ in Edge.

Edge Secure DNS / DoH can bypass the lab resolverIf PowerShell resolves idp.rupakdey.in to 192.168.1.252 but Edge times out, disable Edge Use secure DNS for the lab or enforce a browser policy that uses the system resolver. In this build, Secure DNS resolved the public path instead of the BIND split-DNS answer.
CheckpointExternally, idp.rupakdey.in follows the public CNAME to Skytap. Internally, Windows resolves the same hostname directly to 192.168.1.252. Both paths use the same trusted certificate and canonical OIDC issuer.
Module 6

Federate Keycloak to Zscaler Authentication Service with OIDC

ZscalerAdvanced60–75 min
GoalUse Zscaler Authentication Service / ZIdentity as the central relying party. The Zscaler login domain routes to Keycloak, while Keycloak keeps its independent Safemarch username/email.

1. Protect administrator access first

Before mapping the user domain to an external IdP, verify at least one local/break-glass administrator on the tenant-provided hosted *.zslogin.net namespace. In the validated tenant this was separate from @rdey.zscaler.net. Verify the local admin in a private browser session before continuing.

2. Start the Zscaler Primary IdP object

Go to Administration → Identity → Authentication Service → External Identities → Add Primary IdP and use:

NameSafemarch-Keycloak
Identity VendorOthers
ProtocolOIDC
Login ID Attributezscaler_login
Domainrdey.zscaler.net (example — select the actual user domain)
Input MethodMetadata URL
Metadata URLhttps://idp.rupakdey.in/realms/Safemarch/.well-known/openid-configuration

Click Fetch, then copy the Redirect URI exactly. In the validated personal tenant it is:

https://rdey.zslogin.net/authn/login/oauth2/code/default

3. Create a dedicated confidential OIDC client in Keycloak

In Safemarch → Clients → Create client:

Client typeOpenID Connect
Client IDzscaler-authentication-service-rdey
Client authenticationOn
Standard flowOn
Direct access grantsOff
Implicit flowOff
Service account rolesOff

Set Valid redirect URIs to the exact Zscaler-generated callback; do not use a wildcard.

4. Use a 64-character shared client secret

A previous validation hit CODE_TO_TOKEN_ERROR / invalid_client_credentials after a longer generated secret was truncated in the Zscaler field. Generate a 64-character hexadecimal secret and set the identical value on both sides:

openssl rand -hex 32

In Keycloak use the client's Credentials tab. In Zscaler use the same value with Client Secret Basic. Never put the secret in screenshots or shared notes.

5. Add the zscaler_login claim

Open Clients → zscaler-authentication-service-rdey → Client scopes → dedicated scope → Mappers → Add mapper → User Attribute:

Namezscaler_login
User Attributezscaler_login
Token Claim Namezscaler_login
Claim JSON TypeString
Add to ID tokenOn
Add to access tokenOn
Add to UserInfoOn
MultivaluedOff

6. Evaluate the token before involving Zscaler

Use the client's Evaluate view with Maya. At minimum verify:

{
  "email": "maya.shah@safemarch.com",
  "given_name": "Maya",
  "family_name": "Shah",
  "name": "Maya Shah",
  "zscaler_login": "maya.shah@rdey.zscaler.net"
}

7. Complete the Zscaler OIDC settings

Token Endpoint Authentication MethodClient Secret Basic
Client IDzscaler-authentication-service-rdey
Client SecretThe same 64-character value
Requested Scopesopenid profile email
Login HintOff

Login Hint is intentionally Off. Maya enters maya.shah@rdey.zscaler.net at Zscaler, but authenticates at Keycloak as maya.shah@safemarch.com.

8. Enable JIT provisioning

On the Provisioning tab:

JIT ProvisioningOn
JIT User Group AttributeLeave blank until Module 7
JIT Attributeemail
User AttributePrimary Email

9. Validate through Zscaler Client Connector

On Windows, make sure the client uses 192.168.1.252 for DNS and the browser can open the canonical Keycloak account URL. Browser-Based Authentication can be enabled in the Client Connector platform settings if you want the system browser to handle the IdP flow.

User-facing Zscaler loginKeycloak authentication identity
maya.shah@rdey.zscaler.netmaya.shah@safemarch.com
daniel.lee@rdey.zscaler.netdaniel.lee@safemarch.com
CheckpointZscaler redirects the selected domain to Safemarch-Keycloak, Keycloak authenticates the user, and JIT creates the Zscaler identity with zscaler_login as Login ID and email as Primary Email.
Module 7

Pass Finance and Marketing Group Membership

ClaimsZscalerModerate25–40 min
GoalEmit simple group names from Keycloak and let Authentication Service place Maya and Daniel into Finance/Marketing during JIT authentication.

1. Add a Group Membership mapper

Open the same dedicated client scope and choose Add mapper → By configuration → Group Membership:

Namegroups
Token Claim Namegroups
Full group pathOff
Add to ID tokenOn
Add to access tokenOn
Add to UserInfoOn

2. Review the dedicated scope

At this point it should contain the baseline claims required by the lab. The current client scope screenshot also shows the later session-attribute mappers.

3. Evaluate a generated token

For Daniel, verify:

"groups": [
  "Marketing"
]

4. Tell Zscaler which claim contains groups

Edit Safemarch-Keycloak → Provisioning and set Just-in-time User Group Attribute to groups. Save, then establish a fresh authentication session.

UserZscaler Login IDPrimary EmailExpected group
Mayamaya.shah@rdey.zscaler.netmaya.shah@safemarch.comFinance
Danieldaniel.lee@rdey.zscaler.netdaniel.lee@safemarch.comMarketing
CheckpointMaya and Daniel authenticate through the same Keycloak realm, and Zscaler receives clean group names suitable for policy criteria.
Module 8 · Optional Extension

Pass Department and Employee Type as Session Attributes

IdentityZscalerModerate25–40 min
Scope noteThis extension was validated in the earlier tenant and remains useful, but it is not required for the final DNS/IdP baseline. The personal-tenant federation works without these mappings.

1. Add two User Attribute mappers

In the existing dedicated client scope, add department and employeeType as User Attribute mappers. For each mapper use the same value for User Attribute and Token Claim Name, JSON type String, and add the claim to ID token, access token and UserInfo.

2. Evaluate before changing Zscaler

Maya:
"department": "Finance"
"employeeType": "Employee"

Daniel:
"department": "Marketing"
"employeeType": "Employee"

3. Create and map Zscaler session attributes

Create two String session attributes if they do not exist, then map:

IdP claimZscaler session attribute
departmentDepartment
employeeTypeEmployee Type

Save the IdP and establish a new end-user authentication session; existing sessions do not automatically gain newly mapped values.

CheckpointThe claims can be inspected in the live Zscaler session and used later as policy criteria independently of persistent group membership.

Troubleshooting Matrix

Troubleshoot the boundary that fails. DNS, TLS, Keycloak, Authentication Service and Client Connector can be proven independently; avoid changing several layers at once.

SymptomLikely cause / observationFix or verification
permission denied ... /var/run/docker.sockUser is not in the Docker group.Verify sudo docker ps; run sudo usermod -aG docker $USER; log in again or use newgrp docker.
BIND will not startSyntax, zone or listener error.Run named-checkconf, named-checkzone, journalctl -u bind9 -n 100 and inspect port 53.
Internal DNS works but public names failForwarders or default route unavailable.dig @192.168.1.252 google.com; verify egress and the preserved gateway.
Certbot gets a certificate but cannot install itnginx does not have a matching server_name.Set server_name idp.rupakdey.in, validate/reload nginx, then certbot install --cert-name idp.rupakdey.in.
OIDC discovery redirects to HTTP or advertises :8080/127.0.0.1Canonical hostname or proxy headers are incomplete.Fix KC_HOSTNAME, KC_PROXY_HEADERS=xforwarded, KC_HTTP_ENABLED=true, and explicit HTTPS forwarded headers before federation.
External idp.rupakdey.in works but Office Windows cannot reach itPublic NAT hairpin path is unusable.Prove 192.168.1.252:443, then use the exact-host BIND split zone returning 192.168.1.252.
PowerShell resolves private IP but Edge still times outBrowser Secure DNS / DoH bypasses the system resolver.Disable Edge Use secure DNS for this lab or enforce a policy that uses system DNS; flush DNS and restart the browser.
dig @192.168.1.252 idp.rupakdey.in still returns public IPLocal zone is not loaded.Check named.conf.local, run rndc reconfig and rndc zonestatus idp.rupakdey.in. The final response should carry the aa flag.
Zscaler login immediately says invalid username/password and Keycloak logs show no requestThe external IdP was mapped to the wrong Zscaler domain.Edit Safemarch-Keycloak and select the actual end-user domain, e.g. rdey.zscaler.net. Retest before changing Keycloak.
CODE_TO_TOKEN_ERROR / invalid_client_credentialsClient ID/secret mismatch or a truncated secret.Generate openssl rand -hex 32, use the exact same 64-character value on both sides, and keep Client Secret Basic.
User is JIT-created but has no groupGroup mapper absent, full path undesired, or JIT group attribute missing.Emit groups, set Full group path Off, verify the token, then set JIT User Group Attribute to groups and reauthenticate.
Old-hostname issuer mismatch / invalid redirect appears in Keycloak logsStale browser tabs or sessions still reference the previous IdP hostname.Close old tabs/sessions and use only https://idp.rupakdey.in. Do not troubleshoot the retired hostname as a live federation problem.
ZPA option is missing from the Forwarding Profile; ZCC shows ZPA connection error although authentication succeedsObserved in this lab: the tenant's ZPA entitlement had been removed from the backend. ZCC logs showed zpn_cloud blank and attempted any.broker..Confirm the correct broker name any.broker.prod.zpath.net resolves and TCP/443 works. If the ZPA option is absent from the portal/profile, open Zscaler Support; endpoint reinstall/re-enrollment will not repair a missing backend entitlement.

Useful diagnostic commands

# Services
sudo systemctl status bind9 nginx docker --no-pager
cd /opt/keycloak && docker compose ps

# Ports
sudo ss -lntup | egrep '(:53|:80|:443|:8080)'

# DNS
 dig @192.168.1.252 idp.safemarch.com
 dig @192.168.1.252 google.com
 dig @192.168.1.252 idp.rupakdey.in
 sudo rndc zonestatus idp.rupakdey.in

# nginx / TLS / OIDC
sudo nginx -t
curl -I https://idp.rupakdey.in
curl -s https://idp.rupakdey.in/realms/Safemarch/.well-known/openid-configuration | jq

# Keycloak logs
cd /opt/keycloak
docker compose logs --tail=150 keycloak
docker compose logs --tail=100 postgres

# Windows
Resolve-DnsName idp.rupakdey.in
Test-NetConnection idp.rupakdey.in -Port 443
Resolve-DnsName any.broker.prod.zpath.net
Test-NetConnection any.broker.prod.zpath.net -Port 443
ZCC log interpretation: getZpnAuthState describes the ZPA authentication state; getZpnProxyState describes broker/tunnel connectivity. During the entitlement incident the client could be AUTHENTICATED while the proxy state failed, which prevented unnecessary changes to Keycloak.
